## Kyoto 6-Day Trip Snapshot
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg

A balanced Kyoto plan for **2 adults**, centered on temples, walkable neighborhoods, local food, and **one low-transit reset day**. I’m assuming you want a comfortable pace, public transit plus walking, and no luxury splurges.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Budget
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar.svg

| Day | Focus | Main plan | Est. spend/day | Booking level |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| Apr 10 | Higashiyama arrival walk | Kiyomizu-dera area, Sannenzaka/Ninenzaka, Yasaka Shrine, Gion evening stroll | JPY 24,000 | Mostly flexible |
| Apr 11 | Arashiyama temples and river | Bamboo Grove early, Tenryu-ji, river walk, Togetsukyo, monkey park if desired | JPY 29,000 | Flexible, monkey park optional |
| Apr 12 | Fushimi Inari + sake district | Sunrise at Fushimi Inari, Tofuku-ji or Uji add-on, Fushimi sake tasting/dinner | JPY 26,000 | Flexible |
| Apr 13 | Northern Kyoto temple day | Kinkaku-ji, Ryoan-ji, Ninna-ji, quiet neighborhood food stops | JPY 25,000 | Flexible |
| Apr 14 | Relaxed low-transit day | Nishiki Market, Kyoto Imperial Palace area, cafe time, Pontocho dinner | JPY 22,000 | Keep open |
| Apr 15 | Final temples and departure | Nanzen-ji, Philosopher’s Path if in season, souvenir food run, airport transfer | JPY 18,000 | Flexible |

### Daily Plan Details

#### Day 1: Higashiyama Arrival Walk
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Arrive, check in, then start with **Kiyomizu-dera** and the surrounding lanes.
- Afternoon: Walk **Sannenzaka, Ninenzaka, Yasaka Pagoda area**, and pause for matcha or yuba.
- Evening: Easy **Gion** stroll for atmosphere and dinner.
- Food: Try **yudofu, tofu skin, or obanzai**.
- Spend guide: lodging/transport JPY 14,000; food JPY 7,000; admissions/snacks JPY 3,000.

#### Day 2: Arashiyama Temples and River
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Go early to the **Bamboo Grove** and **Tenryu-ji** before crowds build.
- Afternoon: Walk the river area around **Togetsukyo Bridge**; add the monkey park only if you both feel energetic.
- Evening: Return to central Kyoto for a relaxed dinner.
- Food: Look for **yuba dishes, soba, and grilled skewers**.
- Spend guide: transit JPY 2,000; food JPY 8,000; admissions JPY 4,000; flexible extras JPY 15,000.

#### Day 3: Fushimi Inari and Sake
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/map.svg
- Morning: Start at **Fushimi Inari Taisha** very early for the best walking experience.
- Afternoon: Choose either **Tofuku-ji** for another temple stop or **Uji** for a tea-focused side trip.
- Evening: Head to the **Fushimi sake district** for tasting and dinner.
- Food: Pair dinner with **sake, sake kasu dishes, and local izakaya plates**.
- Spend guide: transit JPY 2,000; food JPY 8,000; admissions/tastings JPY 4,000; flexible extras JPY 12,000.

#### Day 4: Northern Kyoto Temple Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- Morning: Visit **Kinkaku-ji** first, then move to **Ryoan-ji**.
- Afternoon: Continue to **Ninna-ji** and keep the pace slow with tea or dessert stops.
- Evening: Return early and enjoy an unhurried dinner.
- Food: Try **kaiseki lunch if budget allows**, otherwise simple noodle or tofu meals.
- Spend guide: transit JPY 2,000; food JPY 9,000; admissions JPY 4,000; flexible extras JPY 10,000.

#### Day 5: Relaxed Low-Transit Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/moon-stars.svg
- Morning: Sleep in, then browse **Nishiki Market** at an easy pace.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Morning: Sleep in, then browse **Nishiki Market** at an easy pace, Kyoto, Japan
- Afternoon: Visit the **Kyoto Imperial Palace** area or settle into a cafe and shopping break.
- Evening: Dinner in **Pontocho** or a nearby alley with minimal moving around.
- Food: Best day for **street snacks, pickles, tamagoyaki, and sweets**.
- Spend guide: transit JPY 1,000; food JPY 10,000; shopping/snacks JPY 6,000; admissions JPY 1,000.
- This is the best day to keep plans loose and avoid overbooking.

#### Day 6: Final Temples and Departure
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/clock.svg
- Morning: If energy is good, walk **Nanzen-ji** and part of the **Philosopher’s Path**.
- Afternoon: Pick up souvenirs, then head to your departure point.
- Evening: Travel home.
- Food: One last **matcha dessert, soba, or onigiri**.
- Spend guide: transit JPY 3,000; food JPY 6,000; souvenirs JPY 9,000.

## Budget Fit and Booking Priorities
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/currency-rupee.svg

Your total target is **JPY 180,000**, and this plan fits comfortably if you keep lodging moderate and avoid too many premium meals or taxis.

### Budget Estimate for 2 People
- Lodging: **JPY 70,000–90,000**
- Food and drinks: **JPY 45,000–55,000**
- Transit: **JPY 10,000–15,000**
- Temple admissions and small activities: **JPY 12,000–18,000**
- Snacks, coffee, and souvenirs: **JPY 15,000–25,000**

### What to Book Ahead
- **Hotels/ryokan**: book now, especially for April cherry blossom season.
- **Dinner reservations**: book if you want kaiseki, a popular omakase, or a sought-after izakaya.
- **Any private tea ceremony or special experience**: prebook.
- **Airport transfer or reserved-seat train**: book if you prefer a smoother arrival/departure.

### What to Keep Flexible
- Most temple visits
Media: Alt=Most temple visits, Kyoto, Japan
- Neighborhood walking routes
- Cafe stops
- Nishiki Market browsing
- The Uji or Tofuku-ji add-on on Day 3
- Monkey Park on the Arashiyama day
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/ea/Iwatayama_Monkey_Kyoto.jpg Alt=Monkey Park on the Arashiyama day, Kyoto, Japan
